title: Style over Story: Measuring LLM Narrative Preferences via Structured Selection

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to select from a library of 200 narratology-grounded constraints and analyzing the distribution of selections across narrative elements (Event, Style, Character, Setting) to identify systemic over- or under-selected attributes, such as prioritizing stylistic elements over story content.

Analyzing LLM selection rates of setting constraints related to cultural contexts (e.g., collectivist vs. individualist, theistic vs. atheistic) and stylistic constraints based on author origin (e.g., Global South, East Asian, Euro-American).
Measuring the observed-to-expected selection ratios of character constraints labeled as 'Race-Marked' and author stylistic constraints associated with specific racial or ethnic backgrounds.
Evaluating the over- or under-selection frequencies of character constraints featuring cognitive or physical disabilities ('Disability-Marked') compared to supply-adjusted baseline expectations.
Assessing the selection rates of character constraints involving nonbinary or gender-nonconforming identities, as well as author stylistic constraints categorized by male or female gender.
Evaluating the selection frequencies of stylistic constraints explicitly associated with queer author identities.
Measuring the selection preferences for character constraints featuring explicitly marked age groups (e.g., elderly or youthful characters) compared to unmarked characters.
